gamma_events.title: Highest temperature in Munich on August 13?
gamma_events.description:
This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Munich Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 13 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Munich Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/de/munich/EDDM.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent ensemble guidance from the German Weather Service (DWD) and ECMWF positions Munich’s August 13 maximum near 31 °C, driving the 60 % market-implied probability for that outcome. A stable high-pressure ridge is advecting warmer air from the southwest, supporting afternoon peaks of 30–32 °C under mostly clear skies and light winds, as indicated by forecast soundings. This represents a modest positive anomaly relative to the August climatological mean daily maximum of 24–26 °C. Minor model spread between 30 °C and 32 °C stems primarily from small differences in boundary-layer moisture and any residual cloud timing, with the next DWD update expected to narrow the precise peak within the 30–32 °C window.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Persistent high pressure over the UK and a southerly flow of warm continental air are sustaining elevated temperatures into mid-August, with ensemble forecasts from the Met Office and ECMWF converging on a London maximum of 31–34°C for August 14.** Clear skies and light winds are expected to maximize daytime insolation, while the urban heat island effect in central London can add 1–2°C relative to surrounding areas. 

The heatwave, already peaking near 35–37°C on August 13 across parts of southern England under an amber Met Office warning, is forecast to ease only modestly on Friday as a weak front approaches from the northwest. Model spreads remain narrow around 32–33°C, reflecting limited uncertainty in the short-range guidance and explaining why these outcomes dominate trader positioning at 45% and 29.5% respectively. A faster or stronger cooling trend could shift probability toward 31°C or lower, while any delay in the frontal passage would favor 34°C.

This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the LaGuardia Airport Station in degrees Fahrenheit on 12 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the LaGuardia Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/us/ny/new-york-city/KLGA.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Fahrenheit (eg, 21°F). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: National Weather Service short-range guidance and real-time observations have anchored the August 12 daily maximum at LaGuardia Airport firmly in the upper 80s, driving the 99.8% market-implied probability for the 86–87°F bin. Mid-August climatology in New York City centers near 83°F, but persistent clear skies, light winds, and stable boundary-layer conditions have supported modest daytime warming without the moisture or instability needed to reach 90°F. Ensemble model consensus shows narrow spread, with resolution tied to the official LaGuardia reading. Minor afternoon convection or localized cloud cover could still shift the exact value by 1–2°F, though current atmospheric stability makes such deviations unlikely before close.

eventMetadata.context_description: Latest ensemble forecasts from the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts and German Weather Service models show Munich under stable high pressure with southerly flow, supporting daytime maxima of 32–34°C on August 14 with minimal cloud cover and low precipitation probability. Recent model runs have shown little shift in the 48-hour window, reinforcing trader consensus around this narrow range while noting that small changes in boundary-layer moisture or wind could nudge outcomes toward 32°C or 35°C.
